title: A yearly retreat
hookLine: a few days of silence each year
tomorrow: Sofia's back from retreat with a fever. is God mad at her?

cards: Three days, no phone, the permission slip says. Hand it in at the door. To some people that sounds like rest; to others, a sentence.

Why would anyone choose silence on purpose, once a year? No scrolling, no group chat, nothing to show for it on Monday. Jesus's friends got that invitation first, on a day so crowded they hadn't eaten.

teach.h: COME APART, AND REST A LITTLE.
teach.b: In Mark, the apostles come back from their first mission full of stories, and so many people are coming and going that they have no time even to eat.
Jesus says, in the Douay-Rheims: "Come apart into a desert place, and rest a little." Apart, not away for good.
One to tell a friend: they take a boat to the quiet place, and the crowd runs ahead and beats them there. Jesus has compassion and teaches them anyway. Even the first retreat got interrupted.
That's the Catholic retreat: a few days of silence and prayer, often with a guide, so you come back with your attention handed back to you.
Saint Ignatius of Loyola wrote his Spiritual Exercises as a guide for that kind of time, and retreats are still built on them. A neighbor tradition says it too, and far more often.
Jews who keep the Sabbath stop every week.
In the Jewish Publication Society's 1917 translation of the commandments: "Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy." What's shared: stopping is holy.
Rest isn't time stolen from God; it's kept for God. And an honest difference: for Jews who keep it, the Sabbath is a commandment, every week, kept at home and with the community.
A Catholic retreat is chosen, and might come once a year, usually away from home.

how: Catholics make retreats at retreat houses, monasteries or parishes, from a weekend to several days, often in silence and with a director; schools and parishes run retreats for students and families.

o: a few days of silence and prayer, chosen each year
a weekly day of rest commanded in the law
stepping back from the Church for a time

s: a Catholic retreat and the Jewish Sabbath are the same thing with two names
both treat stopping as holy. but the Sabbath is a weekly commandment; a retreat is chosen, maybe yearly.
Jesus invited the apostles to rest on a day they'd had no time to eat
so many were coming and going that they had no time even to eat.
in Mark, the quiet place stayed perfectly quiet
the crowd ran ahead and got there first. Jesus taught them anyway.

games.q: a friend says a silent retreat is just running away from your problems. what does Mark's scene give you to say back?
o: it's apart, not away: you go to rest and come back to the crowd.
she's right; a retreat is meant to leave ordinary life behind for good.
retreats are only for priests and sisters, so it doesn't apply.
games.why: Jesus says come apart and rest a little, then meets the crowd on the other shore. a retreat is a few days apart, so you can come back.

practice: Close your eyes, or rest them on the floor. For these two minutes you're on a very small retreat: no phone, no task, nobody to answer. When a thought pulls at you, let it wait on the far shore.
If you pray, you can hear the line again: come apart, and rest a little.

wordCard.voice: A yearly retreat. A few days of silence and prayer, chosen on purpose, so you return to the crowd rested. Today's word.

orig.note: Greek: a deserted place, the quiet spot Jesus invites the apostles to in Mark 6:31.

carryVoice: Hold on to this: a few days apart, so you can come back. Rest well.
